cells.date: Śaka 1141, Bahudhānya, Pausha, Lunar eclipse = 1219 A.D., January 2, Wednesday. The Śaka year was current.
cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the king. Records the tax-free grant, made by the king, of the mahāgrāma Prāgģuchchi also called Ballā [la]pura consisting of eight-six vṛittis, out of which six were assigned at the rate of two vṛittis each for the learning of Rig-Vēda, etc., for the teaching of Śāstra (Śāstra-vyākhyāna), for the village god Kēśava and the remaining eighty were assigned to the brāhmaṇas. The tank Chōḷasamudra is referred to among the boundaries described in Kannada language.

BIHAR

BHAGALPUR, DISTRICIT

BHAGALPUR SUB-DIVISION

BHĀGALPUR.—Pedestal of an image of Tārā. This and the following items are from Antichak discovered at the excavated site.
cells.remarks: Begins with the Buddhist formula Ye dharmmā hetu prabhavā, etc. Records that the image is the gift of the great devotee Paramō-pāsaka) pratīhāra Udayavara of the Mahā-yāna school, for the attainment of the supreme knowledge by all the creatures having in their front rank, the āchārya, the upādhyāya, mother and father. In characters of about the 12th century.

cells.place: Slab fixed to the wall of a ruined shrine near Vithala temple.
cells.date: Śaka 1474, Paridhāvi, Phālguṇa śu. 1, Monday = 1553 A.D., February 13.
cells.remarks: Registers the sale-deed (Krayapatra) made by Kambham Kāmā-dikshita, son of Ningā-bhața of Putapariti in favour of Hiri Tiru-malarājaya, son of Bāchīrāja Veṅkaṭaya-dēvamahā-arasu relating to the purchase of Koḷaga hiriya-hittu-gōbina-shala situated at Khatchumāviṇa-kate for 100 gadyāṇas. The latter is stated to have purchased the above mentioned land which was once gifted to Rāmu-bhața son of Dōmaṇa-jōyisa by Kṛishṇarāya-mahārāya. Also records that the former has made subsequent grants like 6 muḍi of land to the deity Aluvārīdēva the worship and the management of which was entrusted to the sthānīkas Hirinya Valabhaya and Chika Valabhaya, sons of Ayi-Rāmā-[nu*]jaya with a stipulation that they have to give 2 paḍi of prāsāda each to the person who prepares flower garlands and guards the temple.

cells.remarks: Beginning lost. Records the tax-free gift of some land in favour of the goddess Bhaṭṭā-raki. Obviously of the temple, by the mahā-nagarattār of Kachchippēdu following the royal order (tirumugam) issued at the instance of the [queen] Kōdaippirāṭṭiyār and executed by Vijayanalluṇan of Aluppakkam. The boundaries of the gift land included Karukkamarnda-Bhaṭṭārikar temple at Kidan-daperumāṇsēri, Peruṅgōvaraiyar-tali, Lāva-ṇīśvara [temple] at Mahindrapādi, in characters of about the 11th century A.D.

cells.location: PATNA DISTRICT
cells.place: Loose slabs within the same compound.
cells.remarks: In six fragments. The Sanskrit portion (in verse) describes an emperor (sārvabhauma, name lost) as world famous. Seems to record an undertaking by the ūrār of certain place (name lost) to remit 4726 and odd kalam of paddy to the Tirumalaippalli at Vaigavūr. It is said that the transaction was entered in the revenue register on the date given in the presence of some persons, including Uttamaśōla Brahmamārāyaṉ, Rājēndra-draśōla-Atimūrkkaccheṅgirai, Rājēndra-śōla Mūvali[vāṇarāja] etc. In characters of about the 11th century A.D. Cf. A.R. Ep., 1907, No. 68 ; S.I.I., Vol. XXIII, No. 68.

cells.location: PATNA DISTRICT
cells.place:
THANAVUR TALUK
VALLAM.—E. Gauriyamman temple, maṇḍapa in front of the central shrines, pillar.
cells.remarks: Commences with the meykīrtti of the king, Tirumagal pōla etc. Records an undertaking given by the pārasavas of the fort in the locality including Alattirai Vīraśōlaḻan alias Sōlaṉpērārāchchiyaṉ to contribute one ulakku of a ghee out of the produce from their lands for a perpetual lamp to the deity Kāla-pidāri Kaitalaipūśal-Nangai at Karuṅgalā Vallam in Eriyūr-nādu. This arrangement is said to have been approved by the king from his day-time throne at Viṇṇaṇēri at the request of Kamban-Maṇiyan alias Vikramasiṅga-mūvēndavēlaḻan of Chūralūr in Chūralūrk-kūṟṟam.

cells.location: PATNA DISTRICT
cells.place: A slab in the pavement of Bhūtēśvar temple in the Garhī.
cells.date: Vikrama 1366, Māgha śu. 11, Thursday = 1309 A.D., February 20. f.d.t.. 33
cells.remarks: Records that the sage (tapōdhana) Bhūtēśvara, worshipped the Mahālinga of Mūlāyatana when the world was harassed by the Mlēch-has. Also records that he did severe penance after the Mlēchhas had committed sins (pātakas) nineteen times and he made a new jalādhāra, when the previous one was broken by the Mlēchhas. The writers of the record were Paṁ Vatsarāja and Paṁ Kṣhēmāṁ-dhara. Ibid., Samvat 1997, No. 4; Abhilēkh, No. 181.

cells.remarks: Incomplete, the lower portion of the tablet having been built up in the ground. The extant portion refers to it as the epitaph of (the famous Persian poet) Mirzā Abū Turāb Riżvī Mashhadī, with the pen-name Figrat. Further quotes the Quatrain (rubā'ī) (composed by him) which was on his lips at the time of death, and another one composed by his son (also a famous Persian poet) Mirzā Rażī with the pen-name Dānish. Only one hemistich of the fragment containing the chronogram of the former's death, composed by another poet Muzaffar Husain, by name, is visible. In characters of about the 17th century. Published only partly in Landmarks of the Deccan (Hyderabad, 1927), p. 49.

cells.place: MAHRAULI. Dargah of Quþ Sūr Şāhib. On the northern gate. Tomb of Shāh 'Abdu'l-Haqq Dihlawi on the north-west bank of .Haud Shamsi. Below the dome, north side, inner face. †
cells.remarks: Gives particulars and details of the life and academic and religious career of Shāh 'Abdu'l-Haqq Muhaddith of Delhi a great Traditionist and author of about 100 books on various subjects comprising in all 500,000 lines, He is stated to have acquired proficiency in the Science of Tradition (Hadith) in the Holy Cities (i.e. Mecca and Madīna) under celebrated teachers and divines and and taught in India for 52 years. First date that of his birth and the second that of his death. In characters of about the 17th century. Published. List Hin. Mus. Mon. Delhi Province. Vol. III, p. 71.

cells.date: [A.H. 723], Dhu'l-Hija [20], V.S. 1380 Paușa bā. 7 Tuesday = 1323 A.D., December 20
cells.remarks: Bilingual. Fragmentary. Records the construction on the given date of a well in the town (qaşba) of Petlāwadar (i.e. Petlād) in the neighbourhood of the Tomb of Shaikhu'l Mashā'ikh (name lost), by Hājī Ismā'il (son of) 'Uthmān Shīrāzī, for public use. The builder also obtained a grant of 20 kumbhas of land from Sayyidu'l-Umarā, Badru'd-Din [Abū] Bakr, Amir-i-Kūh, the Muqţa' of Petlāwadar for its upkeep so that the public, local or outsider, may derive comfort and rest therefrom. Also enjoins upon the future Amīrs, Maliks and Hākims to continue the grant of the said land. Ibid., 1915-16, p. 17, pl. XIV b.

cells.place: Prince of Wales Museum. Slabs No. 1. Findspot; Dābhol, Ratnagiri. District
cells.remarks: Records briefly the purport of an order stating that Malik Shurkh 'Ali who was the deputy (Nā'ib) of Afḍal (Khān the minister) by the order of the king, on receiving representations from the public against the unjust practice of the governors (Hukkām) of Dābhol (Dābhola) whereby the entire property and personal effects including gowns and headgears of a person, whether Hindu or Muslim, dying without a heir, were confiscated, accepted their plea and issued an order to his Chief of Guards (Sarnaubat), 'Abdu'r-Rasūl, that by the royal order, the people were exempted (from this practice) and instructions in writing were put up. Cf. Ep. Ind Mos., 1933-34, p 10, pl. V a.
